key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within minutes to hours. LOCATION: DIALYSIS access site or systemic. DURATION: Develops over minutes to hours, may persist for days to weeks. CHARACTER: ACCESS site problems, bleeding, clotting, infection. AGGRAVATING: DIALYSIS, movement. RELIEVING: ACCESS care, medications. TIMING: Sudden onset, develops over minutes to hours. SEVERITY: 6-9/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: ACCESS SITE PROBLEMS, bleeding, clotting, infection, may have fever, may have swelling. KEY POSITIVES: Access site problems, bleeding, clotting, infection, fever. KEY NEGATIVES: No neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

includes.patient_friendly: all at once or very quickly
all at once or very quickly

red_flags: Severe bleeding from access site - possible arterial bleeding, call 911
Signs of severe infection - fever, chills, rigors - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of severe metabolic acidosis - deep breathing, confusion, coma - call 911
Signs of severe electrolyte imbalances - confusion, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias - call 911
